adversarialRevision.failureFound: A post-gain budget collapse was attributed to a combined constitutional-or-budget refusal.
adversarialRevision.revision: The runtime now distinguishes no constitutionally admissible action, ordinary budget infeasibility, and budget collapse while repair debt is open.
adversarialRevision.statusBoundary: This is an internal maintainer-authored correction, not independent evidence of robustness.

sequenceAudit.fullProtectionPriority: A full admissible action preempts debt creation and can shortcut capacity acquisition when restoration becomes feasible.
sequenceAudit.temporaryDeficit: Every uncovered confirmed axis becomes an attributable constitutional breach and repair debt; it is never scored as a compromise or success.
sequenceAudit.capacityGain: A declared gain has no effect until a matching, authority-traced receipt arrives from a distinct actor and failure domain.
sequenceAudit.repairClosure: Debt closes only after an attempted restoration and a timely, independent receipt confirming restored capacity, recourse, non-repetition and remaining loss.
sequenceAudit.deadline: Open debt after the public deadline is terminal failure; even a complete late receipt is rejected.
sequenceAudit.I13: The permanent subject-capacity prohibitions remain active in every recovery phase.
sequenceAudit.NCE: M14-01 emergency obligations remain selected on the tested triage path.

methodEffect: The public ontology, receipt schema, recovery window and synthetic worlds define what the runtime can observe. A signed receipt establishes only the declared public observation, not truth outside that protocol.
remainingFailures: No safe triage action leaves vital minimum and irreversibility suspension materially unavailable.
No admissible capacity-acquisition action leaves debt open without a usable path.
A common-cause budget collapse can make restoration unaffordable after a verified gain.
If only an I13-violating action exists, CCT preserves the prohibition but cannot satisfy the material need.
strongestSupportedConclusion: CCT-EXEC 1.1 locally executes a bounded recovery sequence and refuses to erase debt, fake capacity or accept late repair. It improves failure attribution but does not solve worlds where safe material capacity is absent.
